rows.text: Mortimer exhaled through his nose, a small sound with the administrative weight of a rejected application. The smell of smoked meat lingered, having correctly assessed that nobody here would ask it to leave.
A warm, peppery smell drifted past, making a persuasive argument against having principles before lunch. Mortimer gave a satisfied sniff; goodwill was considerably cheaper to produce than sausage.
The machine gave a small, accusatory hiss. Gerald narrowed his eyes at it; apparently even the equipment needed to earn his respect, and its application was not progressing.
Gerald acknowledges you with a tiny nod as the machine lets out a weary hiss. You have been exempted from his general disapproval, which continues operating at full capacity around you.
A grain of grit skittered past Flick with the confidence of something that had never been asked to justify its place in the budget.
Grit crunched beneath your footsteps beside the fountain. Even the echo was brief, as though anything longer would require approval from someone who had already left.
Portia gave a tiny stone creak, the architectural equivalent of leaving someone on read. Her disapproval had settled into the comfortable permanence usually reserved for temporary restrictions.
Portia gave a small, settling creak as you passed beneath her. Friendship had not stopped the structural complaints, but they were now being filed as suggestions.
Marginalia made a faint chewing noise, with the air of someone whose approval required a processing fee. Dust settled in the silence, apparently content to be the only thing making progress.
A page turned somewhere behind you with the soft, officious rustle of a rule being introduced after you had broken it. The smell of old paper suggested the appeal had already been declined.
A faint clicking followed your footsteps, half a beat late. Even here, reality preferred to register a complaint rather than fix anything.
A dry clicking rose beneath your feet, then stopped with the embarrassed precision of a system discovering that its error had become a feature.
